title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization & Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose:
This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML evaluation practices into a single operational reference covering: eval-harness onboarding, canonical prompt sets and benchmark rules, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profile validation, and the regression triage workflow. The intent is to make onboarding repeatable, reduce regression mean-time-to-resolution, and ensure model changes meet production quality and cost targets.

Scope:
- Applicable to all model onboarding, model variant rollouts, and quantization experiments intended for Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private serving.
- Covers: eval harness configuration, prompt-set design, benchmark construction, acceptance criteria, quantization validation metrics, and regression triage playbook.
- Out of scope: research-only experiments that will not be evaluated against production prompt sets or deployed.

Ownership and Roles:
- Applied ML / Eval Platform: primary owner for eval-harness infra, templates, and guardrails.
- Model Owner (team that ships the model): responsible for prompt sets, onboarding checklist, running evals, and initial triage.
- Observability / SRE: provide monitoring hooks, SLO definitions, and alerting thresholds.
- Product / PO: define critical user-facing tasks and acceptance criteria for rock-solid regressions.

High-level process (onboarding & release):
1) Pre-onboarding: Model owner opens a model-onboarding ticket and attaches model card, target use-cases, and baseline metrics.
2) Prepare evals: create canonical prompt sets (dev, continuous, canary), benchmark templates, and quality criteria (see Prompt Sets section).
3) Baseline run: run the eval-harness against the current production model(s) to capture baseline metrics.
4) Candidate run: run candidate model(s) and quantized variants in the harness; collect delta metrics.
5) Regression analysis: apply automated regression detectors (see thresholds) and human review for flagged tests.
6) Rollout plan: if passes, rollout via canary -> ramp -> full. If fails, execute regression triage.

Prompt sets and benchmark guidelines:
- Prompt set tiers:
  - dev: small, fast-running set for iteration (~200 examples).
  - continuous: broader set used in nightly/regression runs (~2-5k examples depending on task).
  - canary: focused set covering highest-risk user journeys (100-500 examples).
- Construction rules:
  - Each prompt must include metadata: intent, dataset source, expected behavior, and tags (safety, hallucination, formatting).
  - Avoid dataset overlap between dev/continuous/canary sets to prevent leakage.
  - Maintain 1:1 mapping of prompt -> expected reference(s); where multiple valid outputs exist, include canonical scoring rubric.
- Benchmark metrics (per task):
  - Generation tasks: ROUGE-L, BLEU (where applicable), BERTScore, Exact-Match/Task-specific accuracy, and human-evaluated quality for canary.
  - Classification/reranking: Precision@k, Recall@k, NDCG, F1.
  - Safety & hallucination: false positive safety violations, hallucination rate (measured via reference checks).
- Acceptance criteria example:
  - No reduction in production-critical canary metrics by >1.5% absolute for quality metrics, and no increase in hallucination rate >0.5% absolute.
  - Latency P95 must remain within configured SLO (see Monitoring section).

Quantization profiles and validation:
- Recommended quantization tiers: FP16 (baseline for throughput), INT8-PTQ (fast experiments), INT4-QAT (experimental / cost-first).
- Profile metadata (required): target device, per-layer sensitivity notes, expected memory savings, expected token/sec change, recommended eval prompt sets.
- Validation checklist for any quantized variant:
  1) Run a full continuous benchmark suite and compare against baseline.
  2) Run safety guardrails and canary prompts as above.
  3) Run a divergence test: sample 1k prompts, compute token-level divergence and semantic drift (embedding cosine similarity).
  4) Compare latency and peak GPU memory; verify that memory gains are realized without unacceptable quality regressions.
- Quantization red flags:
  - >2% absolute degradation in task accuracy on continuous set.
  - Large semantic drift (mean embedding cosine < 0.93 compared to baseline for retrieval/semantic tasks).
  - Emergent formatting regressions (e.g., missing required JSON fields).

Regression triage playbook (step-by-step):
1) Detection: Automated sentinel tests or nightlies flag a regression. Alerts should include: test id, baseline metric, candidate metric, delta, and associated canary prompts.
2) Triage owner assignment: The model owner is automatically assigned; if unresponsive within 2 hours, escalate to applied-ml on-call.
3) Initial assessment (0-4 hours):
   - Re-run failing tests with the same seed and full logs.
   - Compare raw model outputs; run quick diff scripts to highlight semantic/format changes.
   - Check canary prompts first to prioritize user-facing regressions.
4) Hitlist and rollback decision (4-12 hours):
   - If degradation is broad or severe (meets rollback thresholds in the table below), trigger immediate rollback and open an RCA ticket.
   - If degradation is narrow (single feature/formatting), prepare a fast fix branch and additional targeted tests.
5) Deep analysis (12-72 hours):
   - Run model-attribution and source-of-change diagnostics (token-level attention, prompt-sensitivity studies).
   - Evaluate whether quantization, kernel selection, or runtime changes contributed.
6) Remediation and verification (72+ hours):
   - Deploy fixed candidate to canary and re-run full harness.
   - Close regression ticket only after canary passes acceptance criteria and post-deploy monitoring shows no reversion.

Rollback thresholds (quick-reference):
- Absolute quality drop on canary (production-critical tests): >= 1.5% -> immediate rollback.
- Hallucination increase (absolute): >= 0.5% -> immediate rollback.
- Latency P95 increase over SLO: >= 25% relative -> consider rollback or infrastructure mitigation.
- Increase in customer-facing errors (e.g., malformed JSON) >= 0.2% absolute -> immediate rollback.

Monitoring & alerting (SLOs and signals):
- Suggested SLOs for model serving (per-route):
  - Latency P95 <= 300ms for chat-small routes; <= 800ms for long-context generation.
  - Availability >= 99.9% over 30d.
  - Quality SLO: no more than 0.5% of canary prompts failing safety checks per 7d window.
- Harness alerting signals:
  - Delta-quality > threshold (per-task) -> Pager to applied-ml on-call.
  - Canary-only regressions -> Ticket to model owner + slack notification.
  - Nightly cross-model regressions -> Weekly review meeting if >3 models flagged.

Eval harness configuration example (YAML snippet):
# eval-harness config example
model: "candidate-v2"
reference_models:
  - "prod-stable-v1"
tasks:
  - name: "summarization"
    prompt_set: "canary/summarization-2026-03"
    run_params:
      max_tokens: 512
      temperature: 0.0
      batch_size: 8
    metrics: ["rouge-l","bertscore","human_canary_review"]
  - name: "qa"
    prompt_set: "continuous/qa-2026-01"
    run_params:
      max_tokens: 256
      temperature: 0.0
    metrics: ["exact_match","f1","hallucination_rate"]

Runbook: fast rollback (operational steps)
1) Identify last known-good model tag and create rollback change in serving config.
2) Run quick smoke tests on canary endpoints (run 100 canary prompts).
3) Update traffic routing to point to last-known-good (canary -> 100% within 5-10 minutes for severe regressions).
4) Notify product, SRE, and customers as per escalation playbook.

Templates and artifacts (where to store):
- Prompt sets: /data/evals/prompt-sets/{team}/{task}/{tier}/ with manifest.csv describing fields.
- Quantization profiles: /models/quant-profiles/{model}/{profile-name}.yaml
- Eval run artifacts: /artifacts/evals/{run-id}/ with metrics.json, raw-outputs.json, human-review.csv.

Quality guardrails (quick checklist):
- All canary prompts have human-review labels where applicable.
- Safety classifier coverage run on every candidate.
- Formatting/contract tests (JSON schema) for structured outputs.
- Cost/latency budget annotated in model card.

Escalation contacts:
- Applied ML on-call: #applied-ml-oncall (Slack) and paged via PagerDuty Team: applied-ml.
- SRE on-call: #sre-oncall
- Product-critical alert: email product-leads@redwood.ai

Related pages and reference commands:
- Eval harness infra: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025.json
- Quantization profiles: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026.json
- Regression triage historical RCAs: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/

FAQ (short):
Q: When is human review required?
A: Human review is required for any canary failure that impacts user-facing quality or safety and for final signoff on new quantized profiles.

Q: How do we test runtime-induced regressions?
A: Include kernel/runtime variant as a dimension in the eval-harness config and run an A/B comparison; check for behavior parity and performance metrics.

Contact and support:
For questions about this playbook, open a ticket in the Applied ML project board and tag @aisha.patel. For urgent regressions follow the Escalation contacts above.

Appendix: Example metric table (quick-reference)
Metric | Target | Rollback threshold
------ | ------ | ----------------
Canary quality (task-specific) | match prod baseline +/- 0.5% | >= 1.5% drop
Hallucination rate | < 0.2% absolute | >= 0.5% absolute
Latency P95 | SLO (per-route) | >= 25% over SLO
Memory peak (per-GPU) | <= device capacity - safety buffer | Memory regression causing OOMs -> immediate rollback
